items.headline: Mixed Close on Friday as Tech Weakness Persists Amid Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: U.S. stocks concluded a volatile week with a mixed performance on Friday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted gains, while the S&P 500 saw a minor uptick and the Nasdaq Composite declined, primarily due to continued weakness in technology shares. All major indices finished the week lower, as investor sentiment remained cautious amid concerns over elevated AI spending, ongoing geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East, and new global tariffs. Oil prices fell for the first time in a week, offering some relief on inflation fears.

items.statContext: Rose less than 0.1% (+3.68 points) on Friday.

items.headline: Digital Realty Trust Surges on Strong Q2 Earnings
items.summary: Digital Realty Trust surged nearly 14% following a robust Q2 2026 earnings beat, boosted by raised full-year guidance and analyst upgrades.

items.headline: SLB Posts Strong Q2 Results, Driving Shares Higher
items.summary: SLB N.V. gained 11.01% after reporting better-than-expected second-quarter financial results, driven by strong international offshore drilling growth and expansion in technology-focused businesses.

items.headline: Tenet Healthcare Leads Pre-Market Gains
items.summary: Tenet Healthcare Corporation saw significant gains in pre-market trading, rising over 15%.

items.headline: Sandisk Tumbles Amid Broad Memory Stock Weakness
items.summary: Sandisk Corporation dropped almost 11%, mirroring declines across other memory-related stocks on Friday.

items.headline: Intel Down Despite Earnings Beat on AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: Intel shares declined 7.89% as investors focused on growing concerns over high artificial intelligence (AI) spending plans, looking past a reported quarterly earnings beat.

items.headline: Technology Sector Retreats as AI Spending Worries Persist
items.summary: The technology sector experienced a 2.37% decline on Friday, as investors continued to grapple with concerns over the escalating capital expenditures related to artificial intelligence. Mixed earnings reports from some major tech companies also contributed to the sector's pullback.

items.headline: Oil Prices Ease Slightly, Brent Crude Settles Below $97
items.summary: Brent crude oil prices fell almost 4% to settle at $96.78 a barrel, the first weekly decline after a surge earlier in the week. This dip offered a slight alleviation of inflation fears, though ongoing Middle East tensions continue to underpin energy market volatility.

items.headline: S&P 500 Q2 Earnings Show Strong Growth, Beating Estimates
items.summary: With 27% of S&P 500 companies having reported, Q2 2026 blended earnings growth is at 37.9%, potentially marking the highest growth since Q3 2021. A remarkable 86% of companies have reported actual EPS above estimates, significantly exceeding historical averages.

items.headline: New Tariffs and Middle East Tensions Weigh on Global Market Sentiment
items.summary: New tariffs imposed by the U.S. on goods from 60 countries, replacing expiring ones, coupled with heavy fighting in the Middle East, fueled investor nervousness. These geopolitical and trade risks introduce uncertainty regarding supply chains, input costs, and overall corporate margins.
